title: Seat an SFP module from its slanted holder into a slanted network card's left port
instruction: Take the SFP module out of its slanted holder and push it, tip first, all the way into the network card's left SFP port (the one nearer the left arm).
context: Seating a pluggable SFP transceiver in a network card is a routine data-center hardware step. The module only fits tip first, in line with the port, and turned to match the card. The card leans back 45 degrees in its cradle and stands about 8 degrees off square to the robot, so the hand has to turn the module and follow the port's slanted axis, not push straight down.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), on the station table. Network card: a PCIe card model with a green PCB and steel parts, fixed in a steel cradle that leans it back 45 degrees (top edge toward the arms) and turned 8 degrees counterclockwise (seen from above); only its upper part is modelled, 12 cm wide, 2.1 cm thick, its highest point 12.8 cm above the table, fixed. Its top edge carries two steel SFP ports (cages) whose openings face up and toward the arms along the 45-degree axis: each 16.0 mm wide, 11.0 mm tall and 48.9 mm deep inside, 23.2 mm apart, the middle between the two mouths at x 30, y 8, 11.4 cm above the table. Left port: the one at the larger y. SFP module: a 20 g gold-coloured rigid body, 14 mm wide, 12 mm tall (latch included) and 55 mm long, lying in a fixed steel holder (a plate under its body, two side rails 17 mm apart and an end stop under its tip) that leans it back 45 degrees the same way, tip down and latch end up, its origin at x 22, y 30; its top end is 5.6 cm above the table. Both stand on thin steel base plates. One fixed starting layout.
scoring: Measured on the module's tip: depth is how far its tip is below the port mouth, along the port's axis. 1.0: tip depth at least 42 mm in the left port, with the module within 3 degrees of the port axis and within 3 degrees of the card's turn, and at rest for 1 s. 0.5: depth at least 20 mm in the left port, within 10 degrees of the port axis and of the card's turn. 0.25: depth at least 5 mm in the left port, same angles as 0.5. Otherwise 0. The tip must also be within 1.5 mm of the port's centre line at the mouth, or 4.5 mm once it is inside. Any other outcome scores 0, including the module in the right port or off the table. Real-world check: the part of the module still outside the port is at most 13 mm long at 42 mm depth.
reset_notes: Lay the module back in its holder, tip down against the stop.
fidelity: DRAFT: geometry is the box colliders of the public AIC SFP module and NIC card models (Apache-2.0), at full size, and the slanted holder follows the AIC SFP mount's 45-degree layout in simplified form. Only the card's upper part is modelled. The ports and the bracket slot are widened by 1.0 mm on each side (real clearance is about 0.1 mm, which jams in simulation), so the margin is looser than real: the module clears the port walls by about 1 mm. No latch spring, retention click or electrical contacts, so no insertion force or click. Friction 0.8.
